title: What Will Be The Pivot Point For Policy?
text:
What Will Be The Pivot Point For Policy?

Andrew Batson

Gavekal Dragonomics | 25 Nov 2026

In China, 2026 will go down as another year of deficient domestic demand and disappointing macro policy. The government is again preparing to declare that it has just met its annual GDP growth target of 4.5-5%, a success that is mainly due to another stunning rise in exports. Real growth in domestic demand, though, is now running at less than 3%, similar to the pace in 2024 when the government made a much-publicized “policy pivot” to support growth. But actual policy ultimately did not change much and domestic demand has stayed weak, with the government tinkering at the margins to provide just enough stimulus to meet its growth target. This dynamic persisted despite its costs, which have apparently not been large enough to push the leadership onto a different course.
